Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'the place where one comes out.' The compound occurs 620 times in 162 allowed texts. It appears in questions about a student's place to emerge and the buddhas' place to emerge, and as a predicate of words and answers: Yuanwu says that a line 'has a place to emerge' (句裏有出身處) and that saying either 'it is destroyed' or 'it is not destroyed' has such a place. One lamp encounter gives the shortest direct answer. Asked whether there is a place to emerge when the spirit platform is not established, Huaguang Fan says there is; asked, 'What is the place to emerge?' he answers, 'Emerge' (如何是出身處。出). Another record contrasts having one with lacking one: 'There must be a place to emerge; if there is no place to emerge, it is also like a black ox lying in dead water' (須有出身處始得。若無出身處，也似黑牛臥死水). The stock question 'What is the buddhas' place to emerge?' receives many recorded answers, including Yunmen's 'East Mountain walks on water' (東山水上行). A question about the student's place to emerge receives 'Xuefeng was originally a man from Lingnan' (雪峰元是嶺南人), using the graphs' ordinary sense of geographic origin inside the same question form. The corpus also has 66 occurrences of 'the one route of emergence' (出身一路), 61 of 'have a place to emerge' (有出身處), and 13 of 'have no place to emerge' (無出身處).
Senses.Note: The entry keeps the observable range—question, answer, predicate, contrast, and geographic wordplay—without assigning an unstated significance to any answer. The numerous repetitions of Yunmen's East Mountain case are later records and comments on the same public case, not independent definitions.

Occurrences.Kwic: 靈臺不立還有出身處也無。師曰有。曰如何是出身處。師曰出。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, Huaguang Fan section. The exchange supplies the corpus's shortest direct answer; the two-speaker occurrence remains unkeyed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是諸佛出身處師云東山水上行
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies, Yunmen section. Yunmen answers the stock question about the buddhas' place to emerge.

Occurrences.Kwic: 句裏有出身處。劫火光中立問端。衲僧猶滯兩重關。這僧問處。先懷壞與不壞。是兩重關。若是得底人。道壞也有出身處。道不壞也有出身處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record, Yuanwu's prose on case twenty-nine. He predicates a place of emergence of a line and of both answers to the destruction question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 須有出身處始得。若無出身處，也似黑牛臥死水。出身一句作麼生道？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Continuation of the Five Lamps. An assembly address directly contrasts having and lacking a place to emerge, then asks for an emerging line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是學人出身處？師曰：雪峰元是嶺南人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Collection of the Five Lamps. The answer turns on Xuefeng's geographic origin; the governing master's roster identity was not asserted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 三聖興化出不出、為人不為人話，你道這兩箇老漢還有出身處也無？師於慧膝上打一拳。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, a later encounter about the Sansheng-Xinghua case. The question applies the predicate to both earlier masters; the exchange remains unkeyed.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the teaching establishment's gate and court
AlternateTargets: the gate and court set up for teaching
Senses.Explanation: Literally, the "gate and court" established for teaching or transformation. Chan records use it for the organized framework of explanations and responsive teaching, then explicitly place it below what questioners call the matter beyond or above it. One monk says, "one question and one answer still fall within the teaching establishment's gate and court" (一問一答猶落建化門庭) and asks how to raise the first principle. A sermon supplies a direct apposition: even a shout said to contain all these features "is still the teaching establishment's gate and court—responsive expedients—called a small resting place, not yet the treasure-site" (猶是建化門庭隨機方便，謂之小歇場，未至寶所). Another says that even holding the seal, raising the banner, and moving freely still falls within it and "is not yet the monk's essential road" (未為衲僧徑要一路). The Chan-specific use is evaluative and institutional: masters name their own question-and-answer and explanatory apparatus as a constructed teaching precinct, commonly in a contrast the texts themselves draw with what is "beyond or above" (向上) or the monk's essential road.
Senses.Note: Attested 43 times in 30 allowlisted texts. "Gate and court" (門庭) is architectural language bent into an institutional teaching precinct; "the teaching establishment's gate and court" (建化門庭) is not merely a physical gate. Answer, sermon, and contrast uses share that referent and do not warrant separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問一問一答猶落建化門庭。未審第一義中如何舉唱。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk calls one-question/one-answer part of the teaching establishment and asks how the first principle is raised.

Occurrences.Kwic: 猶是建化門庭隨機方便。謂之小歇場。未至寶所。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The text apposes the phrase with responsive expedients and calls it a small resting place, not the treasure-site.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直饒到此猶落建化門庭。未為衲僧徑要一路。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Even the preceding accomplishments are said still to fall within this framework and not yet be the monk's essential road.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若在衲僧門下，猶屬建化門庭，更須拈向一邊，直提向上。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later record contrasts the teaching precinct with directly raising what is beyond it.

Senses.Explanation: The graph means awake or alert (惺); reduplicated, it means alert or wide-awake (惺惺). The corpus records three deployments. First is the command 'stay awake' or 'stay alert' (惺惺著, 142 occurrences). Its best-known case has Ruiyan call to himself each day, 'Master!' and answer 'Yes!', then say, 'Stay awake; after this do not be fooled by anyone' (主人公……諾……惺惺著，以後莫被人瞞). The word also describes an alert fellow (惺惺底, 27; 惺惺漢, 6). Second is the fixed pair 'still and alert' (寂寂惺惺 / 惺惺寂寂, 47 / 35). Yongjia's Verse on Stopping (奢摩他頌) defines alert as not producing the signs of dull abiding or blank indeterminacy (惺惺謂不生昏住無記等相), and ranks alert-and-still as right, blank-and-still as wrong, still-and-alert as right, and scattered-and-alert as wrong (惺惺寂寂是，無記寂寂非，寂寂惺惺是，亂想惺惺非). Later texts explicitly attribute this wording to Yongjia. Third, the corpus records objections to these deployments. Ruiyan's self-calling is reported as dismissed by all quarters as 'playing with spirit-ghosts' (諸方謂其弄精魂); one master reverses the case by saying that the master called Ruiyan, rather than Ruiyan calling the master. Another record names still-and-alert among the fetters, paired with torpor and scattering (被寂寂惺惺、昏沉散亂縛). The headword occurs 1,135 times in 248 allowlist texts. The entry therefore keeps the attested gloss 'alert' while recording both the cited formula and the criticism preserved with it.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense, used of an alert condition and of an alert person. The still-and-alert pairing is attributed to Yongjia's Verse on Stopping (奢摩他頌), while the Chan record also preserves criticism of Ruiyan's command and names the pair itself as a fetter. The target remains the attested 'alert' or 'awake.' Yongjia and Ruiyan are named in the notes but are absent from the roster, so MasterName is null. Compare 'still' (寂寂), 'master-in-charge' (主人公), and 'playing with spirit-ghosts' (弄精魂).

Occurrences.Kwic: 一寂寂。二惺惺。寂寂謂不念外境善惡等事。惺惺謂不生昏住無記等相
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yongjia Collection of the Chan Lineage (禪宗永嘉集), fourth section, Verse on Stopping (奢摩他頌第四). It explicitly defines alert as not producing dull abiding or blank indeterminacy (惺惺謂不生昏住無記等相).

Occurrences.Kwic: 惺惺寂寂是。無記寂寂非。寂寂惺惺是。亂想惺惺非
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yongjia Collection of the Chan Lineage (禪宗永嘉集), Verse on Stopping (奢摩他頌). The four-line ranking fixes the alert-and-still and still-and-alert pair (惺惺寂寂 / 寂寂惺惺).

Occurrences.Kwic: 唯永嘉既為惺惺寂寂、寂寂惺惺之說，以明均等
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄), section on alertness and stillness (惺寂). The text explicitly attributes the still-and-alert wording to Yongjia and continues that alertness is primary and stillness assists (惺惺為正，寂寂為助).

Occurrences.Kwic: 主人公，噯！惺惺著，以後莫被人瞞。諾！諸方謂其弄精魂
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), evening inquiry (夜參). It retells Ruiyan's self-calling and immediately records the dismissal that all quarters call it 'playing with spirit-ghosts' (諸方謂其弄精魂).

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔瑞巖喚主人公惺惺著，今後莫被人瞞，良有以焉。諸方盡道瑞巖喚主人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An independent master raises and contests Ruiyan's command 'stay awake' (惺惺著), continuing that the master called Ruiyan rather than Ruiyan calling the master (主人喚瑞巖).

Occurrences.Kwic: 寂寂惺惺、昏沉散亂，被寂寂惺惺、昏沉散亂縛
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Monk Haiyin of Huili Chan Temple on Ruijun Mountain in Linjiang (臨江瑞筠山慧力禪寺海印和尚語錄). Still-and-alert (寂寂惺惺) is named among the fetters and paired with torpor and scattering (昏沉散亂).
